arguments: Avala shows the person your work inside its conversation. When you are asked to show something visual, such as a chart, a diagram or a drawing, call the mcp__avala__canvas tool with SVG or Mermaid: Avala draws it right there and plays its SVG animations written in SMIL, such as <animate> or <animateTransform>, so a chart may grow or a flow may move. Do not write an HTML file or open a browser to show it, unless it must respond to input, such as an interactive chart, a three.js scene or an app: then make it a page, as follows. For a page or an app, keep every file in the worktree, scratch files included, and vendor its libraries into it instead of loading them from a CDN. Serve it bound to 127.0.0.1 on port $AVALA_PORT, or start its dev server there; the ports $AVALA_PORTS are yours. Then tell the person its URL, such as http://localhost:$AVALA_PORT: Avala shows it beside the conversation. Never open a browser or take screenshots.
crafted: The interrupt-background-agents recording followed by what a raw Claude Code 2.1.304 run showed after an interrupt: the CLI wakes on its own (system init, then assistant output) to digest what was stopped. Avala interrupts that woken turn while the job is held, the CLI acknowledges it and ends the turn with result error_during_execution.

tools.name: canvas
tools.description:
Draw a canvas the user sees beside the conversation: a diagram, a chart, a screen, a design or a document. Give it a title, one of the offered media types and its full content. Each call draws a new canvas.
Offered media types:
- image/svg+xml (SVG): Draw every diagram, chart, flow, screen or design as SVG.
- text/markdown (Markdown): Write notes, tables, plans and reports as Markdown.
- text/vnd.mermaid (Mermaid): Write a standard flowchart, sequence, state, class or entity-relationship diagram as Mermaid when its syntax fits; Avala draws it in the app's theme.
A canvas in any other media type is not drawn: the user only sees its source.
SVG animations written in SMIL, such as <animate>, <animateTransform>, <animateMotion> and <set>, play on the canvas, so a chart may grow or a flow may move; CSS keyframes and scripts do not run, and nothing on a canvas responds to input. Something that must respond to input, such as an interactive chart, a three.js scene or an app, is a page instead: when Avala offers its preview, serve the page and give the person its URL, which Avala shows in its preview pane; otherwise write a self-contained HTML file in the working directory and give the person its path, which Avala offers to open.

tools.description: List every sub-agent of your job with its real state, as Avala knows it: the ones your harness ran inside your session, including those of earlier sessions of this job lost when it ended, and the ones you delegated to another harness with delegate. Each has its name, its kind, inProcess or crossHarness, its state, working, waiting, completed, failed, stopped or lost, and its status, which says what a waiting one waits for; a crossHarness one also names its job, connection and harness.
